structured.answer: If I do it, it would be at Psagot, in the fund "אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)", number 5112628. The page says that with 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month, 70,000 ₪ in all, I'd have 86,045 ₪ after ten years. But that red minus "−0.04%" under that same fund worries me, and I'd ask you or the bank before I put a shekel in.

stuck.why: It opens with מדד and English letters like MSCI and S&P 500. I would have left if I hadn't been given this job.
"−1,030 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם": a minus. I couldn't tell if that's a loss or just a difference.
"−0.04% בשנה · שנה אחת": a minus under the fund that's been chosen for me. Did it lose money? I stopped there.
I wasn't sure what the smaller number under each amount was (1,049, 4,506...). I think it's what the bank takes.

findings.what: A minus sign next to the recommended fund (−0.04%) with no sentence saying what it means. It frightens me off.
The page opens with English letters and מדד, not with anything about saving safely. Someone like me leaves.
A dark background, and the grey text is hard to read even enlarged.
"−1,030 ₪" in the box next to the chosen one. It isn't clear whether that's a loss.
The coloured bar has colours that are close to each other, and I can't tell what each one is.
It doesn't say anywhere that this isn't safe like a deposit and could fall.
A lot of numbers and lists, and it makes me anxious.
